profile.headline: Software Engineer at Probity Inc.

positions.title: Embedded Systems Undergraduate Researcher
positions.description: Participating in a semester-long research project using Field Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGA) and microprocessor-based embedded systems on Radio Frequency (RF) applications. I will be conducting FPGA hardware acceleration on machine learning algorithms using OpenCL to target the board and comparing efficiency with Nvidia high-performance GPUs. Additionally, I will be using Verilog for designing, testing, and debugging as well as programming scripts in a Linux environment to automate measurements.

company.name: Hume Center for National Security and Technology at Virginia Tech

positions.title: Connected and Automated Vehicles (CAV) Sub-Team Member
positions.description:
This semester, I was tasked with modeling vehicle interactions in different traffic scenarios. Using Matlab and Simulink, I discovered how to gather camera and sensor specifications to identify the field of views of each camera/sensor around the vehicle. This will help with sensor fusion and processing algorithms used in the future combined with Deep Learning. 

With the competition requiring Level 2 SAE automation, I researched ACC algorithm and policies, and how the team can be able to utilize cameras, radar, and other sensors to achieve this primary goal of lateral and longitudinal control. Using a test bench scenario, I assisted in developing C code to perform various ACC scenarios.

company.name: The Hybrid Electric Vehicle Team at Virginia Tech

positions.title: Software Engineer Intern
positions.description:
During my twelve-weeks, I successfully developed a custom log file parser in Python to output in JSON to consolidate manual parsing done by external programs in order to be used for data analytics purposes. This project was delivered one week earlier than expected due to the engagement of Agile Scrum development processes and excellent project implementation. 

Additionally, I was able to explore the migration of a local Excel tool used to track aircraft part defects using AWS S3 for the data dump and designing a front-end GUI using PyQt to allow for querying by management and increased usability by shop floor. I was able to create a design architect and communicate effectively with the customer through my exposure to project management skills

positions.title: Machine Learning Student Researcher
positions.description: As an undergraduate student researcher, I was investigating adversarial artificial intelligence and machine learning on vehicle cybersecurity with the mentorship of my research advisor and company sponsor technical leads. I programmed a convolutional neural network model using Python and TensorFlow to classify a large traffic sign image dataset, which resulted in 95% model accuracy through training and testing. I also used various data augmentation techniques, such as salt-and-pepper and image rotations, to validate neural network accuracy at 90%.

projects.title: inVenTs High-Powered Rocketry Team
projects.description: As a member of the electrical subteam, I was responsible for integrating motor hardware and flaps of the drag system within Arduino programming to allow for seamless deployment once the 3,000-meter apogee is reached. Additionally, I improved data logging efficiency by 30% taken from Arduino sensors and data shields by eliminating redundancy in the code. By collaborating with the aerospace and mechanical sub-teams, I ensured that hardware electrical bay design met the bay tube constraint for placing the Arduino hardware inside the rocket.
